rationale: The Court is likely to affirm on AEDPA grounds, emphasizing Musladin/Woodall/White v. Woodall limits on treating generalized “fundamental unfairness” language as clearly established law outside the holding’s context, and alternatively that any such standard leaves room for fairminded disagreement under Yarborough/Lockyer. The Chief Justice is best positioned to write a narrow, institutionally framed opinion, with a substantial chance of a Sotomayor or Kagan dissent (and possible Thomas concurrence) sharpening the step-one/step-two AEDPA dispute.
